exposure: maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection at the time of admission for delivery
cohort: The cohort consisted of 360 women admitted for labor and delivery at the Obstetrics Department of Anhui Provincial Hospital, China, who had a singleton vaginal birth between December 1-31, 2022.
finding: A positive maternal SARS-CoV-2 test in labor among women having vaginal birth was associated with a slightly longer duration of labor, increased likelihood of episiotomy, increased incidence of grade III meconium-stained amniotic fluid, a longer postpartum hospital stay, and a lower rate of breastfeeding 1 week postpartum.
mod_finding: A positive maternal SARS-CoV-2 test was associated with an increased likelihood of episiotomy during vaginal birth.
